title: Eye
summary: The eye is the body's camera - it lets in light through a lens, focuses it, and turns it into signals the brain reads as sight. Explore its key parts and the journey of light.

compareCandidate.label: Eye vs. camera
compareCandidate.description: The eye and a camera work very alike: a lens focuses light onto a light-sensitive surface (retina or film/sensor). But the eye can focus automatically, moves in its socket, and its signal is processed by a living brain.

processes: Turning light into signals on the retina
plainLanguageExplanation: The eye works like a camera. Light enters through the clear front (cornea) and passes through a hole called the pupil, whose size is controlled by the colored iris. The lens behind the pupil focuses the light onto the back of the eye, a screen called the retina. The retina is covered with light-sensing cells that turn light into signals. Those signals travel through the optic nerve to the brain, which builds the picture you see. The eyeball sits in a protective socket, and the sclera is its tough white outer coat. This whole path - light in, focused, sensed, sent - is how you see.

whyItMatters: The eye lets you experience the world through sight. Understanding its parts explains why you need glasses, why pupils change size, and how light becomes the images your brain sees.
didYouKnow: Your eyes capture light and send about 10 million bits of information to your brain every second.
